mcp.selectedContract: One local stdio bridge supports modern 2026-07-28 and legacy 2025-11-25 through wire negotiation. It implements core tools only, projects exact operation contracts, and invokes one selected application adapter without provider-specific runtime code.
mcp.modernBoundary: Modern arbitrary JSON result support and optional MCP extensions are deferred until a separately reviewed modern-only profile. The initial dual-era profile uses object-root inputs and results.
mcp.implementationRecheck: Required at every MCP-affecting work unit and update; material drift stops the work unit.

transportAndGuidanceDecisions.reason: Provides direct CLI behavior and structured introspection without provider registration.
Both reviewed providers support local stdio and MCP keeps execution separate from guidance.
Provider descriptions can reliably activate application-authored outcome procedures while execution still occurs through exact registered MCP operations.
A procedure does not provide executable identity, schemas, byte integrity, registration, permission, or transport.
Instructions may describe the tool category and cross-tool rules but do not own outcome procedures.
The first implementation needs one common local transport and explicit registration authority.

authorityBoundary: This evidence records reviewed current provider and protocol contracts. It registers nothing, initializes no capability, trusts no workspace, grants no permission, starts no process, and authorizes no implementation.
freshnessPolicy: Recheck every authoritative source at the start of the affected work unit and every explicit update. Material contract drift requires reviewed design change.
